text:
EAGAN, Minn. -- The Minnesota Vikings have once again hopped on their quarterback carousel. Backup Carson Wentz will start Monday night's game against the Buffalo Bills, coach Kevin O'Connell announced Thursday, because starter Kyler Murray is nursing a strained hamstring.

The change marks the 14th time the Vikings have shifted from one quarterback to another during a season, either because of injuries or for performance reasons, since Kirk Cousins tore his right Achilles tendon midway through the 2023 season.

"I've enjoyed being here," Wentz said. "I enjoy this offense, enjoy this team, enjoy working with [O'Connell] and I'm excited for another opportunity."

Murray suffered the injury while running on a read-option play early in the fourth quarter of the Vikings' 19-15 loss Sunday to the Detroit Lions. Murray also struggled to connect with open receivers throughout the game, leaving receiver Justin Jefferson so frustrated that he declined to speak with reporters afterward.

O'Connell said that putting Murray on injured reserve is not a consideration.

"I don't believe it to be much more than a week-to-week kind of thing right now," O'Connell said. "But for him, his movement skills and the way he plays the game, we do feel like we'd be putting him at risk of possibly turning this into a more significant injury than it is by trying to have him work through it here early on."

Murray scrambled seven times during a Week 4 game against the New Orleans Saints but has run only 13 times in his five remaining starts. O'Connell said the injury would affect more than simply his ability to run.

"It's more the explosive movements, the quick-twitch movements," O'Connell said. "Running is obviously a part of some of that ... but it's more of just the overall ability to impact the game. And ultimately, we could try to say all we want of, 'Hey, you can play, but you just got to stay in the pocket.' But then football starts, and it's an imperfect game where he's going to react and we don't want to make this strain any worse than it is."

Murray missed most of two games earlier this season because of a concussion, and his QBR (44.7) ranks No. 26 out of 30 qualified quarterbacks as he plays on a one-year contract. Speaking Monday, O'Connell said that Murray would remain his starter this week if he were healthy. Asked Thursday if Wentz had an opportunity to earn additional starts based on his performance, independent of Murray's health, O'Connell said in part: "It's all about this week for our team."

Wentz has started six games and played most of a seventh since signing with the Vikings in August 2025. The team is 4-3 in those games during which Wentz has completed 63.9% of his passes for 1,492 yards, nine touchdowns and five interceptions.

He has excelled in getting the ball to Jefferson, however. In those seven games, Jefferson has caught 44 passes for 615 yards and two touchdowns.

"[Wentz] is the perfect guy in a moment where you can't have Kyler out there at full strength to go in there," O'Connell said. "And we feel very strongly about when Carson's in there, we're going to get really effective quarterback play."

text:
Despite a 6-1 record, Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray's starting job is in question due to poor offensive performance.

New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo is dealing with a hamstring injury, leading to a potential backfield shakeup.

The Minnesota Vikings sit atop the NFC North with a 6-1 record, but quarterback Kyler Murray will miss the team’s showdown against the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football with a hamstring injury and faces mounting questions about his long-term job security.

The Vikings’ winning record masks a subpar offense that ranks 27th in the league, averaging just 20 points per game. Production relies heavily on a dominant defense allowing a league-low 13.3 points per game, rather than a potent passing attack.

Murray looks uncomfortable in head coach Kevin O’Connell’s system, where the former Arizona Cardinals’ franchise quarterback has thrown for just 1,022 yards, five touchdowns and three interceptions through six games while struggling with downfield consistency and timing.

Murray’s hold on the position is tenuous.

The Vikings’ front office limited its financial risk by signing him to a low-cost, one-year “prove-it” contract, leaving the franchise with no long-term obligation if his subpar play persists. Speculation is intensifying following a Week 8 loss to the Detroit Lions, especially with Murray ruled out for Week 9.

Carson Wentz could secure the starting job permanently.

Cam Skattebo injury sparks Giants backfield shakeup

Cam Skattebo remains central to the New York Giants’ plans, but a lingering hamstring injury complicates his availability heading into a Week 9 road game against the reeling Philadelphia Eagles.

The former Arizona State running back was limited to side work with trainers after exacerbating the injury on Oct. 25 during an explosive overtime run against Houston. The Giants had a bye last week. John Harbaugh characterized Skattebo’s status as day-to-day.

Skattebo hadn't practiced as of Thursday morning, Nov. 5.

The backfield crunch is amplified by Tyrone Tracy Jr. landing on injured reserve with a hamstring strain. With Tracy sidelined for at least four games, veteran Devin Singletary projects to carry the bulk of the workload if Skattebo is limited. The Giants also signed Greg Desrosiers Jr. off the Los Angeles Chargers’ practice squad to the active roster.

Seahawks integrate Quenton Nelson after Colts selloff

The Seattle Seahawks are reshaping their offensive line after acquiring left guard Quenton Nelson from the Indianapolis Colts.

Seattle sent a third-round selection and a 2028 fifth-round pick to Indianapolis to secure the elite blocker, who made his Seahawks debut in a loss to the Chicago Bears on Monday Night Football. Analysts expect Seattle to offset the draft-capital loss with future compensatory picks.

Nelson provides immediate protection for the reigning Super Bowl champs, who have ruled out quarterback Sam Darnold for their Week 9 game against the Cardinals. Drew Lock is expected to start.

Nelson should also help open running lanes for Jadarian Price, Zach Charbonnet, Emanuel Wilson and George Holani.

Rashee Rice solidifies role in Chiefs’ passing game

Rashee Rice returned to play last week against the Denver Broncos after missing two games with a strained right hamstring and a lingering knee injury.

The wide receiver immediately re-energized a stagnant offense, hauling in seven of his eight targets for 53 yards and a touchdown. His presence ended a glaring drought for Patrick Mahomes, who had failed to throw a touchdown pass during Rice’s two-week absence.

Kansas City fell to its division rival, 28–24, marking the team’s second consecutive loss. But Rice’s health and immediate production provided a critical silver lining as the Chiefs prepare for a Week 9 matchup against the New York Jets.

Purdy maintains MVP pace despite Niners injuries

Brock Purdy keeps his offense operating at an elite level despite a persistent wave of injuries to his supporting cast.

The Gilbert Perry grad protects the football, avoids sacks with precise pocket movement and delivers accurate throws under pressure. His ability to elevate the roster keeps him at the forefront of the NFL MVP conversation entering Week 9, along with Buffalo Bills superstar Josh Allen, despite dealing with an injury-depleted receiving corps.

Purdy led the 49ers to a 6–1 start before their Week 8 bye. Through his first seven games, he has completed 69.2% of his passes for 1,748 yards, racking up 15 passing touchdowns against just four interceptions. He also has a league-leading 79.3 QBR and an impressive 110.1 passer rating. The Niners host the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday.

text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals and Seattle Seahawks both saw a handful of changes to their Week 9 injury report after Thursday's slate of practices.

Most notably, Quenton Nelson was downgraded from limited to DNP in Seattle while Earnest Jones was added today with an ankle injury. In Arizona, majority of their rest guys returned to practice (Josh Sweat, Budda Baker among others), while Max Melton was added with a knee injury.

Arizona Cardinals Injury Report

DNP: Jacoby Brissett (other), Bam Knight (concussion), Jon Gaines (ankle), Jayden Williams (knee)

LIMITED: Walter Nolen (ankle), Michael Wilson (ribs), Isaiah Adams (ankle), Max Melton (knee)

FULL: Reggie Virgil (back), Budda Baker (rest), Hjalte Froholdt (rest), Josh Sweat (rest), Isaac Seumalo (rest)

With so many injuries in Arizona's running back room, LaFleur was down to only one running back last Sunday in Dallas.

Who would have been the emergency back? While LaFleur will have more resources this week, he pointed to wide receiver Devin Duvernay.

"I know it crossed my mind, but it was what it was. And so, if ‘TA ‘would’ve started cramping and needed to come out, we would’ve had to make a decision within 10 seconds of 'who was going to go back there," LaFleur said.

"We would’ve made it and you guys would’ve thought we were ready for it, but we weren’t. We would’ve just flown and guess what? Whoever would’ve went back there, again, I’ll just keep using (WR Devin) Duvernay because that’s who comes to the top of my head, he would’ve stepped up and done whatever he could.”

Seattle Seahawks Injury Report

DNP: Derick Hall (back), Charles Cross (ankle), Sam Darnold (quad/ribs), Connor O'Toole (foot), Brandon Pili (back), Rashid Shaheed (knee), Leonard Williams (stinger), Quenton Nelson (knee)

LIMITED: Anthony Bradford (knee), Velus Jones (hamstring), Drew Lock (right elbow), Uchenna Nwosu (ankle), Ernest Jones (ankle)

FULL: Nick Emmanwori (shoulder), Tory Horton (hand)

LaFleur says their Week 2 film will be especially helpful preparing for Drew Lock as Darnold has been ruled out for now a second contest against Arizona this season.

“No, it’s valuable. You can see the stuff he liked and what they had success with. Obviously, a lot has changed since Week 2. The first week is what it is. Week 2, you’re still kind of trying to find yourself and you’re not really even settled in yet as a team by any means. But yes, we can use that as a benefit for sure," he said this week.

Both teams will practice once more on Friday before revealing official game designations such as out, questionable or doubtful.

title: Why isn't Lamar Jackson playing today? Injury update, return timeline for Ravens QB
description:
Jackson suffered a thumb injury that is expected to sideline him long-term.
Here's everything you need to know about Jackson's thumb injury and when he might return to the field.
Jackson suffered a thumb injury in the Ravens' Week 8 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
"That'll be a surgery deal," Minter said when discussing Jackson's injury during a postgame news conference on Sunday, Nov. 1.
Brissett has previous experience working with Ravens quarterback coach Israel Woolfork during their time together with the Arizona Cardinals.
text:
The Baltimore Ravens are taking on the Jacksonville Jaguars in a "Thursday Night Football" game that could prove crucial for their chances of staying in the AFC North race.

The Ravens will have to navigate that game, and the foreseeable future, without the services of their starting quarterback, Lamar Jackson.

Jackson suffered a thumb injury that is expected to sideline him long-term. This marks the second time this season the veteran quarterback is facing a multi-game absence, after missing three games leading up to Baltimore's Week 8 game against the Buffalo Bills with an ankle injury.

Here's everything you need to know about Jackson's thumb injury and when he might return to the field.

What happened to Lamar Jackson?

Jackson suffered a thumb injury in the Ravens' Week 8 loss to the Buffalo Bills.

The injury occurred on Jackson's first passing attempt of the game, when he hit his throwing hand on the arm of Bills pass rusher Gregory Rousseau. Jackson immediately reached for his hand in pain and was seen clutching it while running toward the sideline.

Jackson was quickly deemed out for the remainder of the game. He was later spotted wearing a cast on his injured hand after he returned to the field clad in street clothes during the second half of the contest.

Before the game against Buffalo, Jackson had missed the previous three games because of an ankle injury. He has appeared in five of the Ravens' eight games this season but has only finished three.

How long is Lamar Jackson out?

The Ravens have not provided a definitive timeline for Jackson's return, but coach Jesse Minter confirmed the star quarterback will be placed on IR because of his thumb injury.

"That'll be a surgery deal," Minter said when discussing Jackson's injury during a postgame news conference on Sunday, Nov. 1. "He'll go to IR. That's a tough deal."

Players placed on IR must miss a minimum of four games, per NFL rules. That would guarantee Jackson misses the Ravens' Weeks 9-12 games before becoming eligible to return for their Week 14 contest against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, which comes after their Week 13 bye.

But Minter did acknowledge that Jackson's injury could "potentially" be season-ending. He also declined to provide updates about the quarterback's thumb when asked during a Monday, Nov. 2 news conference.

"I'm not going to get into the specifics of the injury," Minter told reporters.

Minter did reveal Jackson had not yet had surgery to repair his thumb malady and that the Ravens would likely have a more concrete update about his status "maybe sometime this week."

Is Lamar Jackson out for the season?

The Ravens have not yet clarified whether Jackson will be able to return during the 2026 NFL season. Minter simply said the injury was "potentially" season-ending but did not offer a concrete timeline for the veteran quarterback's return.

Who is the Ravens' starting QB?

Normally, veteran Tyler Huntley would take on that mantle in Jackson's absence. However, he is dealing with a turf toe injury and is expected to miss the rest of the season because of it.

That has left third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano to serve as the starter for "Thursday Night Football" in Week 9. The undrafted rookie spent the final three seasons of his college career at UConn and completed 68% of his passes for 3,448 yards, 28 touchdowns and one interception during his sixth and final college season.

Fagnano (6-3, 230 pounds) completed 10 of 21 passes for 91 yards and an interception in relief of Jackson and Huntley against the Bills.

That said, Fagnano isn't expected to be the Ravens' long-term starter. The team has agreed to acquire veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett in a trade with the Arizona Cardinals, and Brissett will assume the starting mantle beginning in Week 10, if all goes well.

Brissett has previous experience working with Ravens quarterback coach Israel Woolfork during their time together with the Arizona Cardinals.

Ravens QB depth chart

Baltimore's quarterback depth chart remains in flux with Jackson and Huntley out and Brissett not yet officially acquired.

Brissett is expected to top the Ravens' quarterback depth chart once he officially joins the team, but below is a look at the pecking order within the group for Thursday's game.

Joe Fagnano

Austin Reed (practice squad)

Kedon Slovis

Reed signed to the Ravens' practice squad on Monday, Nov. 2, just after Jackson and Huntley's injury. The 2024 undrafted free agent previously played for the Chicago Bears but has never appeared in NFL regular-season game. The Western Kentucky product thrived for the Dallas Renegades during the 2026 UFL season, completing 56.3% of his passes for 1,923 yards, a league-high 21 touchdowns and nine interceptions.

Slovis is another player who went undrafted in 2024. The USC, Pitt and BYU product spent time with four NFL teams before joining the Ravens from the Packers' practice squad. He dressed for two games with the Arizona Cardinals last season and completed 1 of 2 passes for negative-2 yards.

Because Slovis was on the Packers' practice squad, the Ravens needed to sign him to their 53-man roster to obtain him ahead of Thursday's game. That said, the 25-year-old will likely remain behind Reed given that the latter spent time with Baltimore during the preseason – though Slovis, like Brissett, previously played for Woolfork in Arizona.

authors: Brady Henderson, Dan Wetzel, Mike Kaye, Nick Wagoner, Nate Taylor, DJ Bien-Aime, Jeremy Fowler, Mel Kiper Jr, Jordan Reid, Michael A. Fletcher
description:

The Seahawks plan to start Lock on Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals because of Darnold's right quadiceps injury.
But Lock has been dealing with an injury to his right elbow for at least the past 3½ weeks.

Lock, though, said Thursday that he was "expecting to go take every rep" for the rest of the week.
text:
RENTON, Wash. -- Seattle Seahawks backup quarterback Drew Lock, who's in line to start this week with Sam Darnold sidelined, says the elbow injury that made him inactive for the past two games is "doing a lot better."

"It's doing good," Lock said Thursday. "I'm excited to be back out there. Felt great to get under center, rip some balls yesterday. Feels good."

The Seahawks plan to start Lock on Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals because of Darnold's right quadiceps injury. But Lock has been dealing with an injury to his right elbow for at least the past 3½ weeks. He was listed as a limited participant all week, including Thursday, by the Seahawks, and relegated to the role of emergency third quarterback the past two games.

Lock said Thursday that he would not have been able to start the past two games if Darnold had been unavailable, and that his throwing in practice those weeks was limited to individual periods. He was not seen throwing on the field during warmups alongside Darnold and QB3 Jalen Milroe before either of the past two games.

Coach Mike Macdonald said Wednesday that the Seahawks would also get Milroe ready to play this week in case he needed to step in against Arizona, and that Lock's throws will be managed in practice. Lock, though, said Thursday that he was "expecting to go take every rep" for the rest of the week.

"I'm going at it like a normal week," he said. "If the training staff want to pull it back a little bit, then we'll let them make that decision."

Lock first appeared on Seattle's injury report on Oct. 11. Macdonald on Wednesday said he was hurt during a rainy practice, though he did not specify when or how. Lock did not provide details when asked how his injury occurred.

This will be Lock's second time this season leading Seattle's offense. He played most of the first two games after Darnold sustained a glute injury on the fifth play of the opener. In wins over the New England Patriots and Cardinals, the eighth-year veteran completed almost 73% of his passes, with four touchdown passes, zero turnovers and the league's sixth-best Total QBR (82.5) in that span.

His three touchdown passes helped Seattle beat Arizona 31-7 at State Farm Stadium.

"I'm really excited, especially after a couple weeks of not throwing too much," he said. "Being able to get out in the huddle with the guys and throw the football and spin it around. Any chance you get to go out there and do that, it's an exciting time."

Darnold injured his quad near the end of the Seahawks' 34-17 loss to the Chicago Bears on Monday night, which dropped the reigning Super Bowl champions to 4-4. Macdonald said he's week-to-week and that he won't be put on injured reserve.

Macdonald revealed Wednesday that Darnold also sustained a cracked rib when he was hit by blitzing cornerback Kyler Gordon on the second play against Chicago.

"I didn't know the extent of it, but after going through a whole season and having a hawkeye on him for most of all those games, I could tell pretty early that it was bothering him," Lock said. "He was an absolute soldier out there playing through that, and my hat goes off to him. It just shows how much he cares about this football team, how much he loves football and what he's willing to do for us. It's a special thing from a starting quarterback."

title: Jets' Breece Hall says he's ready to play, cites threats for social media exit - ESPN
authors: Rich Cimini, Mike Clay, Matt Bowen, Dan Wetzel, Mike Kaye, Nick Wagoner, Nate Taylor, DJ Bien-Aime, Jeremy Fowler, Brady Henderson
description:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- New York Jets running back Breece Hall proclaimed himself ready to play Sunday after missing five games because of a quadriceps injury -- a difficult period in which he received hostile messages on social media.
He said people were angry because he didn't play the past two games after being listed as questionable.
Hall said he has a "love-hate relationship with Jets fans, and that's part of being an athlete in New York.
"I'm still a starter, still a very good running back in this league," Hall said.
As for the trade rumors, Hall shrugged them off, knowing they come with the territory.
text:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- New York Jets running back Breece Hall proclaimed himself ready to play Sunday after missing five games because of a quadriceps injury -- a difficult period in which he received hostile messages on social media.

Hall deleted his accounts, fueling speculation he was on the verge of being traded. The reason, he said, was because people were questioning the validity of his injury, which he said was more serious than reported.

He said people were angry because he didn't play the past two games after being listed as questionable. In both cases, he practiced on a limited basis but wasn't ruled out until game day. He practiced fully Thursday for the first time since the injury.

"I've had people threatening me and my family on social media," he said. "So that's not something that's good for your mental health that you should be looking at. So I'm just like, all right, if people think it's that serious, if you're willing to go that low, then it's like nothing that I need to look at."

Hall said he has a "love-hate relationship with Jets fans, and that's part of being an athlete in New York. You have to deal with that because they want you to be available, they want you to play, they want you to play very well. So it is what it is."

While he was rehabbing his injury, Hall watched backup Braelon Allen go on a tear, rushing for 504 yards over the five games -- second-most in the NFL in that span. Not only did it spark trade rumors, but it has raised questions about Hall's role as the Jets' No. 1 running back.

Offensive coordinator Frank Reich reiterated the team's position Thursday, saying Hall remains the No. 1 back. The Jets signed him to a three-year, $43.5 million contract in the offseason, following several months of trade speculation.

"We have some plays that are tagged for one or the other, but it's a great problem to have," Reich said. "You've got two No. 1 backs. Breece is, obviously ... our guy, but it'll be a mix."

The Jets (2-6), losers of three straight, face the Kansas City Chiefs (5-2) at Arrowhead Stadium.

"I'm still a starter, still a very good running back in this league," Hall said. "Obviously, Braelon's been playing good. I think him and the offense have caught their stride after the first three, four games. So it's going to be good to just get in there, just play some ball."

Hall said he has no issue sharing the workload with Allen, whom Reich called a "phenomenal player."

"I've always been the advocate of when Braelon comes in," Hall said. "He loves the ball, so that's never been a problem for me. I think it's just been a product of the O-line starting to play really well and Braelon's been playing really well. So I think no matter who's in there is going to be successful."

Hall returned to practice two weeks ago, but his quad still was getting "inflamed" and "really sore and stiff" the day after practices. He said he decided not to push it and risk re-injury, knowing Allen was performing well.

As for the trade rumors, Hall shrugged them off, knowing they come with the territory.

"It's like if I have 100 yards, they love me," he said. "If I don't, everybody's like, 'Get him out of here.'"

text:
Backup quarterbacks — and even some third-stringers — have taken their fair share of regular season snaps throughout the first half of the 2026 NFL season. Several quarterback injuries are forcing teams across the league to turn to their backups once again in Week 9.

Seven teams will be starting backup quarterbacks, including five that will be starting their first game of the season.

The Baltimore Ravens are turning to undrafted rookie quarterback Joey Fagnano, who was serving as their emergency third-string option until starter Lamar Jackson and backup Tyler Huntley both suffered significant injuries in a nightmarish 36-10 loss against the Buffalo Bills in Week 8. Baltimore is finalizing a trade with the Arizona Cardinals for quarterback Jacoby Brissett, but the transaction won't be processed in time for their matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday Night Football.

The Seattle Seahawks are expecting to start quarterback Drew Lock after starter Sam Darnold suffered a quad injury during Monday night's game against the Chicago Bears. Lock was forced into action earlier this season after Darnold suffered a glute injury in the season opener. He led Seattle to a 13-10 victory over the New England Patriots in Week 1 and defeated the Arizona Cardinals in a 31-7 blowout in Week 2.

Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders is expected to make his season debut against the New Orleans Saints. Starting quarterback Deshaun Watson has led the Browns to an impressive 5-3 record, but he entered the NFL's concussion protocol after reporting concussion symptoms to the team on Tuesday.

Quarterback Joe Milton will make his first career start for the Philadelphia Eagles, who benched backup quarterback Tanner McKee following a 27-10 loss against the Washington Commanders. The Eagles have lost six consecutive games, including all three of McKee's starts.

Arizona Cardinals quarterback Gardner Minshew earned the starting role after he stepped in and led his team to an electric comeback against the Dallas Cowboys last Sunday. Although Brissett, who was benched during the game, was traded to Baltimore earlier this week, Minshew may not have a long leash with rookie quarterback Carson Beck waiting in the wings.

Quarterback J.J. McCarthy will make his second start for the New York Giants after leading them to a 27-21 overtime victory against the Houston Texans. The Giants acquired the third-year passer in a trade with the Minnesota Vikings after losing quarterback Jaxson Dart to a season-ending injury, and McCarthy replaced backup Jameis Winston, who was benched during a Week 6 loss.

The Minnesota Vikings will start quarterback Carson Wentz for a primetime matchup against the Buffalo Bills on Monday night after starter Kyler Murray was ruled out with a hamstring injury. Wentz previously stepped in to provide relief after Murray suffered a concussion in the team's regular-season opener. Although Wentz helped Minnesota pick up a pair of victories over their first two games, the credit for the team's success largely belongs to their top-ranked defense.

description:

The Rams got more good news when outside linebacker Myles Garrett (knee) returned to practice as a limited participant.

text:
Rams coach Sean McVay wouldn’t allow much about the ice pack on quarterback Matthew Stafford’s arm after Sunday’s win over the Chargers other than to say it was soreness. The injury report said it isn’t serious, and Stafford agreed.

Stafford was a full participant, listed with an elbow injury.

“I’m 38 years old, trying to keep up with these young bucks. Little bit of soreness and stuff that is not uncommon this time of year,” Stafford said, via Gary Klein of the Los Angeles Times. “Haven’t missed a rep. Feel good. So I’m not too worried about it.”

Stafford underwent surgery on his elbow during the 2022 offseason.

He threw only 25 passes on Sunday.

The Rams got more good news when outside linebacker Myles Garrett (knee) returned to practice as a limited participant. It was the first practice Garrett and Aaron Donald have had together.

Garrett underwent arthroscopic knee surgery in mid-September after playing 40 snaps in the season opener. He was given a six-week prognosis and has missed seven games.

The Rams practiced without cornerback Jaylen Watson (shoulder), long snapper Joe Cardona (ankle), cornerback Trent McDuffie (back), tight end Colby Parkinson (ribs) and safety Kam Curl (foot) on Wednesday.

Inside linebacker Grant Stuard (hamstring), offensive lineman Steve Avila (hamstring), wide receiver Jordan Whittington (back) and tight end Terrance Ferguson (ankle) were limited.

text:
The New England Patriots opened preparations for Sunday's game against the Green Bay Packers with several important offensive players missing practice.

Wide receiver A.J. Brown, tight end Hunter Henry and running back TreVeyon Henderson did not participate Wednesday, according to the Patriots' official injury report. Brown was listed with ankle and knee issues, Henry with a foot injury and Henderson with an illness.

Defensive tackle Christian Barmore also missed practice because of illness, while several other New England players were limited.

The report does not establish who will be available Sunday, but it creates a significant storyline for an offense preparing to face a challenging Green Bay defense.

Maye Could Need More Help From His Supporting Cast

Brown's absence is particularly important because the veteran receiver was expected to provide New England with a dependable top target. His season already has been interrupted by injury, and Wednesday's report indicates that his availability remains worth monitoring.

Henry has been another important option for Maye, particularly when New England needs a reliable target in the middle of the field. Henderson provides speed and versatility in the backfield, giving the Patriots a different dimension alongside their other running backs.

Missing all three would require adjustments from offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels. New England could lean more heavily on available receivers, reserve tight ends and its remaining running backs.

Those changes would become particularly important against a Green Bay defense featuring Micah Parsons.

MORE: Ravens Trading for Ex-Patriots QB Could Impact New England's Playoff Chances

Thursday's Practice Becomes Important

The Patriots still have multiple practices before Sunday, and a Wednesday absence does not automatically mean a player will miss the game.

New England will be watching whether Brown, Henry and Henderson return to the field or remain unavailable as the week progresses. The team also will monitor Barmore, whose presence matters along the defensive front.

The Packers have injury questions of their own, including Parsons, who was limited Wednesday with a knee issue.

For New England, the larger concern is maintaining offensive balance. Maye has the ability to make difficult throws, but protecting him and giving him dependable options remain essential.

The Patriots will have a better picture of their available personnel after the next two practices. Until then, Wednesday's injury report provides an early warning that Sunday's offensive game plan could require some flexibility.

text:
After holding a walkthrough on Wednesday, the Detroit Lions (5-2) returned to the practice field on Thursday as they prepare to take on the Miami Dolphins (1-6). While Wednesday’s report was just estimates from the coaching staff, Thursday’s practice mirrored the same level of participation for most players, with a couple of upgrades.

With that in mind, here’s Thursday’s injury report and what we know.

Note: Any changes from the most recent injury report will be bolded.

No practice

C Cade Mays (ankle) — Preparing for Juice Scruggs to start

EDGE DJ Wonnum (concussion)

LB Jack Campbell (neck)

CB D.J. Reed (hip)

Earlier in the week, coach Dan Campbell suggested Mays might miss Wednesday and Thursday’s practices, so this isn’t a surprise, but it’s still unclear whether he can return on Friday. Campbell said the team is preparing to start Scruggs this week, but nothing is finalized.

Wonnum is still in the NFL’s concussion protocol, and while he still has a chance to pass the protocols this week, his lack of return to practice suggests he is a bit further back than hoped.

No updates on Campbell since Wednesday.

Reed said he was in a good spot in his post-game media availability last Sunday, so his absence from practice could mean his injury was worse than he realized or that the team is giving the veteran extra time to be ready. We’ll find out more on Friday.

Limited practice

RB Jacob Saylors (neck)

WR Amon-Ra St. Brown (rib)

S Kerby Joseph (knee, PUP) — Days remaining in injury evaluation clock: 12

Saylors popped up on last week’s injury report with a neck injury and was also forced from the game because of it, but getting in practice reps is a good sign he’s headed in the right direction.

St. Brown got a little banged up in Week 7, but it’s rare to see him scale back even a little, so it’s not surprising that he was back on the practice field this week, and expectations are that he is on track to play against the Dolphins.

In the locker room on Thursday, St. Brown said he was injured on his non-touchdown catch (the play that was overturned), but added, “I’m a little banged up, but I’ll be alright.”

Joseph is expanding his practice exposure this week, but the team is not going to rush him back, and Campbell has already said they don’t plan to activate him this week. He still has 12 days left in his injury evaluation window, which could put him in play for the Lions-Patriots game in Germany, or potentially the following week when they host the Bucs.

Full practice

LB Amen Ogbongbemiga (toe) - Upgrade from Wednesday

CB Rock Ya-Sin (cramps)

S Brian Branch (concussion) - Upgrade from Wednesday

Ogbongbemiga did not appear to suffer an injury in Week 7, but he showed up on this week’s injury report with a toe injury. Not much is known about this injury, but getting in a full practice is a good sign he may be able to play on Sunday. If not, the Lions did add two linebackers to the active roster this week and another to the practice squad, in case the team needs more depth.

Ya-Sin was added to the injury report with “cramps,” suggesting he required fluids, but there shouldn’t be too much to worry about long term as long as he manages his hydration.

Branch is making steady progress through the NFL’s concussion protocols and was on the practice field on Thursday, suggesting he is positioning himself to play on Sunday. He still has steps to clear, including clearance from an independent doctor, but things look on track for now.

text:
November 5, 2026

The Buccaneers are following a progressive plan this week in an effort to get wide receiver Emeka Egbuka on the field Sunday night in Chicago, an Egbuka took the necessary next step in that plan on Thursday.

The Bucs' preparations for the Bears began on Wednesdy but Egbuka did not take part in practice, instead running on an adjacent field with team trainers. After that workout, Head Coach Todd Bowles said the second-year pass-catcher could do more on Thursday if he reacted well to his running session.

"He was out [Wednesday]," said Bowles. "We'll see how he's feeling from the running [today], and we'll try and do more tomorrow to have a better idea."

The Buccaneers' official injury report with a practice status for Egbuka – full or limited – will be released later on Thursday afternoon but in the portion of practice open to the media he was taking part in all drills. He would be deemed a full participant if he also participated in team drills later in the practice.

(UPDATE: Egbuka was, in fact, a full participant in practice on Thursday.)

Egbuka missed the Buccaneers' Week Seven game at Carolina due to win foot and concussion injuries. He then cleared the NFL's concussion protocol last week but his foot injury still kept him out of the Week Eight clash against Atlanta. That proved to be a relatively minor problem because the Bucs ended up throwing only three passes in their 16-0 win while running for a team-record 324 yards on a very rainy afternoon. That game plan, however, is unlikely to be duplicated and the Buccaneers will be seeking a more balanced offense against the Bears, with Egbuka potentially playing an important role.

Egbuka leads the Buccaneers in receptions (28) and touchdown catches (two) and is second with 240 receiving yards despite missing those two contests.

CLICK HERE for a detailed preview of Sunday night's game at Soldier Field.

November 4 Updates

The Buccaneers drafted LSU tight end Bauer Sharp in the sixth round in April, believing he could develop into a productive pass-catcher with decent blocking skills. That process wasn't necessarily going to happen quickly, as the team paid Cade Otton handsomely in the offseason to continue to be the starting tight end a player who generally is on the field for about 95% of the offensive snaps. The team also already had Payne Durham, who proved to be a strong blocker in two-TE sets in 2025, and Ko Kieft, who plays limited offensive snaps but is a tone-setter when he's on the field.

So it wasn't much of a surprise when Sharp only played 22 offensive snaps through the first six games of the season, instead contributing very heavily on special teams. Similarly the Bucs' two fifth-round picks, defensive lineman DeMonte Capehart and guard Billy Schrauth, have yet to take a snap this season. Sharp nabbed his first NFL reception, a 21-yarder, against Pittsburgh in Week Six but to date that is still his only catch.

But something unexpected has developed as the Buccaneers have started directing all their offensive attention to running the ball. Remarkably, the Bucs ran for a combined 584 yards in consecutive wins over Carolina and Atlanta, and Bauer had a hand in that production. He played 15 offensive snaps at Carolina and then 19 against the Falcons this past Sunday as the Bucs utilized two and three-TE formations to great effect. Along the way, Sharp has drawn praise from multiple team sources for his blocking, which seems destined to earn him more playing time going forward. And that added playing time will eventually lead to more production for Sharp in the passing game as the Bucs are able to put multiple tight ends on the field without giving away their run/pass intentions.

"It's kind of been just adjusting and adapting," said quarterback Baker Mayfield. "We thought Bauer was kind of going to be more of a receiving tight end. He's proven that he's a physical player for us and can do the execution on the run plays and do some of the dirty work for us. Obviously, the last couple weeks we're riding the hot hand of the run game, and it's been great with the '12,' '13' personnel, to have your sets. Just being able to be versatile is great for us. Just got to continue to grow it."

Bauer was already in a developmental process when he arrived in Tampa, as he is relatively new to the tight end position. He initially went to Southeastern Louisiana to play quarterback but after a redshirt season switched to tight end while still also being used a Wildcat quarterback. He would later transfer to Oklahoma and then LSU to play tight end for one season each. Learning to block at his new position was surely a challenging transition but it appears he can excel in that area in the NFL.

"Bauer came in and did a great job," said head Coach Todd Bowles. "I think all of them – Cade, Ko, Payne – all of them are doing a great job. Bauer came in and played a lot of snaps the last game and did an excellent job of fitting up in there and understanding that. Knowing he's more than just an athlete and a pass receiver and he can do those types of things really helps us."

text:
The Minnesota Vikings (6-1) are making a change at starting quarterback. Coach Kevin O'Connell announced Thursday that Kyler Murray has a "hamstring strain" and veteran backup Carson Wentz will start for the Vikings against the Buffalo Bills (6-1) on "Monday Night Football" in Week 9.

O'Connell said Murray is considered "week-to-week," but they didn't want to put "him at risk of possibly turning this into a more significant injury." Thus, Wentz will get his second start of the season with Max Brosmer serving as his backup.

"Obviously, there is a ton of confidence in Carson," O'Connell said Thursday. "He's already helped us. Had a major, major role in two wins this year against two really good teams. He's a steadying presence and a guy we know can go in and play good football."

To O'Connell's point, the 33-year-old journeyman performed well in the two games he played filling in for Murray after he suffered a concussion in Week 1 against the Green Bay Packers. Wentz came off the bench in the season opener to throw for 133 yards and three touchdowns on 12-of-19 passing in a 39-22 victory. In Week 2, he started the game at the Chicago Bears, and he completed 11 of his 20 throws for 143 yards in a 9-3 rain-soaked victory at Soldier Field.

Murray, however, hasn't fit well in O'Connell's scheme this season. Murray's -0.11 expected points added (EPA) per dropback is the fifth worst in the entire NFL, ahead of only Cam Ward (-0.12), Tanner McKee (-0.13), Daniel Jones (-0.19) and Justin Herbert (-0.22). O'Connell's offense thrived with Kirk Cousins and Sam Darnold heaving the ball deep down the field to Jefferson and others over the middle of the field. Murray entered 2026 ranking 40th out of 45 qualified quarterbacks in throws of 10-22 yards (intermediate throws) between the numbers (over the middle of the field) in 2025. That's why his connection with Marvin Harrison Jr. failed in Arizona.

Just 10.7% of his throws in 2025 with the Cardinals traveled 10 or more air yards downfield, which ranked third among 42 quarterbacks with at least 150 passes last season. This season playing for O'Connell, 34.4% of Murray's throws are traveling 10 or more air yards, which is the 10th-highest rate in the NFL.

The lack of scheme fit between O'Connell and Murray is why the Vikings offense has just 12 touchdowns in seven games this season, the fewest touchdowns by a team with a 6-1 record or better through seven games since Washington in 1982. The only team that has scored fewer touchdowns than the Vikings in 2026 is the winless Los Angeles Chargers with nine. Both the tanking Miami Dolphins (13 touchdowns) and the Deshaun Watson-led Cleveland Browns (13 touchdowns) have found the end zone more often than O'Connell's unit.

Wentz has a cushy matchup against the Bills in Week 9, with Buffalo entering the week allowing the third-most passing yards per game (254.7) in the entire NFL in 2026.

text:
Apologies on my tardiness with this. I felt we needed a firm update on Jack Campbell before going forward with anything. We got a positive update from Campbell himself yesterday, so let’s go through a somber Week 8 in the NFL.

Jack Campbell, TJ Hockenson, and Sam LaPorta

Sunday started so well. We had a reunion in Detroit with two of the best tight ends the Hawks have produced in the last ten years plus an All-Pro in Campbell. Hockenson found the end zone again, his third touchdown of the year, in a 4-reception, 58-yard day. LaPorta finished with 1 carry for 2 yards plus 3 receptions for 33 yards as Detroit handed Minnesota their first loss of the season, 19-15.

None of that matters at all, as Campbell was left severely injured in the fourth quarter trying to tackle Hockenson. I won’t link to the tackle. No need. You probably all saw it once and you don’t need to see it again. Campbell was motionless on the field for over 10 minutes, leaving his teammates clearly affected and in tears.

Then led to the speculation and fear phase of this. No one knew what was going on with Campbell. Forget his playing career - will he be able to lead a normal life? That’s all that matters here. News was sparse and updates from the Lions were uncertain. Then we heard from Campbell himself and WHEW…some positive news!

That’s about as good an update as we can get. Again, I don’t care about his playing career. If Campbell plays again, it’s a bonus. That is a great update and it sounds like he’ll be ok. We’ll keep an eye out for more updates on Campbell as they’re provided.

Amani Hooker

The big standout this week was Hooker. He’s stuck with this bad 1-7 Tennessee team (to their credit, they’ve shown proof of life at times this season.) And going to Cincinnati, that felt like a blow out was on the schedule for the Titans. They hung and lost in overtime, 43-36, and they hung in part due to Hooker. He finished with 6 tackles and 3 passes defended. He intercepted all 3 passes he defended.

Those picks were worth a little scratch for Hooker. Nice bonus! And we still have a lot of football left this year. Can he get to six picks?

Drew Stevens

A little love for Stevens this week, who’s finding a nice groove now in his rookie year. Stevens made 4 of 5 field goals in Washington’s win over Philadelphia Sunday night (can we get the NFC East out of primetime? Thanks…) That included this 56-yard bomb.

Lukas Van Ness

Another good week at the office for Hercules, as the Packers defensive end started Week 8 last Thursday with 6 tackles, 1 sack, and 1 tackle for loss in a 27-19 win over Carolina. Van Ness is now at 4.5 sacks on the season, which is a career-high.

Tristan Wirfs

We’ll finish with the big man. Did anyone watch this game? Tampa Bay defeated Atlanta, 16-0, in a rain-soaked day in Tampa. Tampa completed zero passes in the game, the first time an NFL team has won a game without completing a pass since 1974. Wirfs was instrumental in the run game, as the Bucs rushed for 324 yards in the win. Wirfs earned a PFF run block grade of 85.9.

text:
The San Francisco 49ers could have defensive end Nick Bosa back on the field for the first time in seven weeks on Sunday against the Las Vegas Raiders, and running back Christian McCaffrey could play, too, despite a left hamstring injury that cropped up in Week 7.

Coming out of the 49ers' bye week, Bosa practiced Wednesday for the first time since injuring his left calf in practice six weeks ago and was listed as a limited participant.

"I feel great," he said. "I'm ready to go."

McCaffrey and wide receiver Mike Evans, who is battling right Achilles tendinitis, did not practice Wednesday, but coach Kyle Shanahan said the team hopes McCaffrey will be able to practice on a limited basis Thursday.

McCaffrey, whose leg went "dead" in the game against the Atlanta Falcons with what he first thought was a thigh injury, sounded confident about his chances to face the Raiders.

"I had no idea (it was a hamstring injury)," he said Wednesday. "Sometimes the adrenaline and all these other things can get to you. … It wasn't too bad. Having the bye week was awesome. But now I feel great."

Deebo Samuel is not likely to return this week as he continues to recover from a right hamstring injury suffered in Week 5 at Seattle, but fellow wide receiver Demarcus Robinson could play after practicing for the first time since injuring his ankle in Week 2 against Miami. Shanahan said Evans "made a lot of progress" over the bye week, while Samuel seems a little further off.

The 49ers have been so depleted at wide receiver that they nearly traded for old friend Jauan Jennings. Shanahan indicated the team agreed to the framework of a trade with Minnesota, saying he arranged a FaceTime call with Jennings through the Vikings.

"We love Jauan," Shanahan said: "He ended up saying he was happy with where he was. It wasn't just like a definite no at first, but he was like, 'Man, Kyle, I'm pretty happy here, I'm liking stuff.' When I heard the way he talked, and with where we're at, I agreed with him."

The team also opened the practice window for cornerback Nate Hobbs (groin), while safety Marques Sigle (ankle) returned to practice. Both were listed as limited on Wednesday, as was nickelback Upton Stout.

title: Where does Jack Campbell's injury stand? Medical expert weighs in after crucial update

text:
Based on the information that has been made public, there are reasons to stay positive about Jack Campbell’s recovery.

Dr. Ari Berg, Spine Surgeon at Hackensack Meridian Health, told The Post on Thursday that while it’s unclear what specific injury and the severity of which Campbell has suffered, the movement in his legs is “definitely encouraging.”

Dr. Berg also offered some insight into why Campbell regained movement in his lower body before his upper body.

The four-year linebacker gave an update Wednesday that he has “full movement” in his lower body and is “continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body” in what were his first comments since the scary neck injury suffered on Sunday.

It’s possible that Campbell has central cord syndrome, which occurs when someone hyperextends his or her neck that causes bruising or a “stinger” to the center of the spinal cord that’s behind the bones of the neck, Dr. Berg explained.

“At the very center of the spinal cord is where you have control of the arms,” Berg said. “More toward the periphery of the spinal cord, you have control of the legs and that’s why when you have this contusion of the center of the spinal cord, it’s more common that you see this weakness in the arms and the upper extremities more so than the legs.”

Dr. Berg added there is good news in that it’s an incomplete spinal cord injury, meaning the spinal cord appears to be fully intact.

As far as the recovery timeline, especially regarding upper-body movement, it’s predicted on a case by case basis. Time also needs to be allowed for the swelling to go down to evaluate his prognosis, Dr. Berg explained.

“[The] long-term prognosis is still, we still need a little bit more information before we can make that judgement,” he said, before adding that Campbell has his “work cut out for him” regarding rehab.

“It could be weeks. It could be months. It could take longer than that. It’s just too soon to call,” Dr. Berg went on. “Again, encouraging that he’s already shown improvements and hopefully he continues on that upper trajectory.”

Still, the 26-year-old has a chance to make a complete recovery as some patients do. Others may have some residual deficits, which depends on the magnitude of the injury and impact on one’s spinal cord.

USA Today’s medical reports added that central cord syndrome can be very painful for patients and cause arms and hands sensitive to touch, as well as greatly diminish one’s grip strength.

During the fourth quarter of the Lions’ 19-15 win the Vikings, Campbell attempted to tackle Minnesota tight end TJ Hockenson when his neck and back seemed to crunch.

He was then put in a stretcher and rushed to a local Detroit hospital in an ambulance.

In Campbell’s statement released by the Lions, he added he remains “very optimistic” and is taking “things one day at a time.”

Campbell, who has a 4-month-old son Cooper with his wife Megan, is currently in his fourth NFL season after he was taken with the No. 18 overall pick in the 2023 draft to Detroit.

Across seven games this season, he has 57 tackles.

The Lions (5-2) are on the road to face the Dolphins (1-6) on Sunday afternoon.

text:
The Seattle Seahawks will be without quarterback Sam Darnold for at least one more game during the 2026 season. The quarterback will surprisingly miss the team's Week 9 game against the Arizona Cardinals due to a quad injury, Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald announced Wednesday.

It will mark the second time this season Darnold has been ruled out vs. the Cardinals. He missed the Week 2 matchup against the team due to a glute injury.

The news comes after Darnold completed 17 of 34 passes for 188 yards and two touchdowns in a 34-17 loss to the Chicago Bears on Monday. Darnold also threw an interception during the contest.

Darnold was able to finish the game and was on the field for the Seahawks' final offensive play of the night. The quarterback, however, picked up the quad injury at some point near the end of the contest, per Macdonald. It's unclear exactly when Darnold sustained the injury.

It wasn't the only injury he dealt with vs. the Bears. Darnold also cracked a rib on the game's second play. That could explain why Darnold struggled with his accuracy during the game. His 50 percent completion percentage was his lowest of the season if you include his 1 for 2 performance in Week 1.

With Darnold out in Week 9, the Seahawks will once again turn to backup Drew Lock … who is also dealing with an injury. Despite an injured elbow that's held him out of the last two games, however, Lock is expected to start against the Cardinals in Week 9.

He was excellent against the team in Week 2, going 19 of 26 for 235 yards and three touchdowns in a 31-7 win. While it initially looked like Lock was in for a longer stint as the team's starter, Darnold was able to return from his glute issue faster than expected, and was able to start for the team in Week 3.

Lock apparently got out of that game unscathed, as his elbow issue didn't pop up on the team's injury report until Week 6, when it was initially ruled a forearm injury. It was classified as an elbow injury ahead of Week 7. Lock was also listed on the team's injury report with an elbow issue ahead of Week 8.

Despite the injury, Lock has been listed as a limited participant in practices over the past three weeks. On the off-chance Lock is unable to go, the Seahawks would be forced to turn to Jalen Milroe.

Darnold's injury comes at an inopportune time for Seattle. Following the team's loss in Week 8, the Seahawks sit at 4-4 on the season. If the playoffs started today, the team would not make the postseason.

Because of that, the Seahawks need to make a second-half push if the team wants to defend its Super Bowl title. While there's still plenty of season left, a loss to the Cardinals in Week 9 would be a significant blow to the team's playoff chances.

title: Jacoby Brissett trade: Ravens strike deal for Cardinals QB amid injury crisis - CBS Sports
description:
The Baltimore Ravens are adding another quarterback to lead a room that has been devastated by injuries, according to ESPN.
Baltimore has agreed to trade for Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett.
Two-time NFL MVP Lamar Jackson suffered a thumb injury that required surgery on his first pass attempt against the Buffalo Bills on Sunday.
This is the second time he has been traded in his career, and the Ravens mark his seventh team.
The Ravens have allowed 10 points fewer per game (22.6) in that same span.
text:
The Baltimore Ravens are adding another quarterback to lead a room that has been devastated by injuries, according to ESPN. Baltimore has agreed to trade for Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett. The deal is expected to be completed this weekend, and compensation has not been finalized.

Two-time NFL MVP Lamar Jackson suffered a thumb injury that required surgery on his first pass attempt against the Buffalo Bills on Sunday. It could potentially be a season-ending injury. Jackson's backup, Tyler Huntley, came in and suffered a season-ending turf toe injury, leaving undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano as the likely candidate to start the Ravens' Week 9 matchup against Trevor Lawrence and the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday night. However, he is also dealing with an ankle injury.

Brissett has spent the past two seasons in Arizona. The Cardinals recently demoted him from starter to third-stringer after Gardner Minshew came in on Sunday, threw three touchdowns, and helped Arizona eliminate a 14-point deficit in the fourth quarter to defeat the Dallas Cowboys in overtime, 33-30. Brissett completed 10 of 23 passes for 119 yards and one interception before being replaced.

Brissett, who turns 34 next month, has completed 63.3% of his passes for 1,719 yards, 10 touchdowns and seven interceptions in eight games this season. CBS Sports Research points out that his 75.6 yards per game to star tight end Trey McBride entering Week 8 were the most by a QB-TE combo since 1970 (min. 15 games). This is the second time he has been traded in his career, and the Ravens mark his seventh team.

While Brissett can't replace what Jackson brought to this Ravens offense, he is an experienced quarterback who has started 73 games (23-50) and thrown 86 more touchdowns than the rest of the Ravens' healthy quarterbacks combined. His 1.5% career interception percentage is also tied for second-lowest in NFL history behind Aaron Rodgers' 1.4%.

Brissett is one of five quarterbacks in the past 365 days to throw for 4,000 yards and 25 touchdowns, joining a list that includes Drake Maye, Matthew Stafford, Jared Goff and Dak Prescott. He also upgrades his own situation. Over the last calendar year, the Cardinals have allowed 32.6 points per game -- which is four points higher than any other team in the NFL. The Ravens have allowed 10 points fewer per game (22.6) in that same span.

Baltimore sits in the basement of the AFC North at 4-4, but hope a veteran under center can propel the Ravens to a playoff spot.

title: What spine experts say about Lions LB Jack Campbell's neck injury update - USA Today

text:
By all available accounts, Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell has avoided the worst in the aftermath of the significant neck injury that resulted in him being immobilized while loaded onto a stretcher and transported to a local hospital during a game against the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 1.

The good news came from Campbell himself, with the 2025 All-Pro releasing a statement Nov. 4 saying he has "full movement" in his lower body and is making progress in an effort to regain movement in his upper body. He also thanked his medical care team at Henry Ford Hospital along with the Lions’ medical staff.

“I’m incredibly encouraged by the progress I’ve made in such a short period of time,” Jack Campbell said in the statement.

Head coach Dan Campbell told reporters that everybody’s positive thoughts, well wishes and prayers were working. But the Campbells (no relation) aren’t alone in the positive outlook.

Medical experts surveyed by USA TODAY Sports concur that the available information about Campbell’s recovery can only be qualified as good news – while offering a window into why might the linebacker have regained movement in his lower body before his upper body.

Dr. Darryl Lau, a neurosurgeon at NYU Langone’s Spine Center where he’s the director of spinal neurosurgery research, said that the spinal cord appears to be intact based on public updates. While Lau hasn't seen Campbell's medical information, he said Campbell having movement in his arms and legs is another optimistic factor.

“And it’s only within days, so those are all positive things,” Lau told USA TODAY Sports, adding that Campbell being a young, professional athlete gives him better odds of recovering than an average person.

The injury occurred because of the hyperextension of Campbell’s head and neck area as he collided with the left hip of Minnesota Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson. That hyperextension can “ding” the spinal cord, according to Dr. Betsy Grunch, a neurosurgeon based in Georgia with more than 1.3 million followers for her Instagram account “@ladyspinedoc.”

Grunch said a hit like that could damage the central part of the spinal cord and cause swelling that asymmetrically affects the arms more than the legs, as Campbell's statement described. Both doctors said the result is a rare injury called “central cord syndrome."

“Typically, (patients) can even have full function in the legs and even greater motor loss in the arms,” Grunch told USA TODAY Sports.

What is Central Cord Syndrome?

Central cord syndrome “looks like a pretty severe spinal cord injury” and certainly can be serious, Lau said. In some cases, Grunch said, it can be extremely painful, with the arms and hands becoming sensitive to touch. A patient’s grip is severely diminished. It’s common in people with spinal injuries who have fallen forward and land on their forehead and extend backward, similar to the action exhibited by Campbell’s head and neck at impact.

“I think it’s great news (if it’s central cord syndrome) because it’s an incomplete spinal-cord injury,” Grunch said, “and if he’s already recovering as quickly as reported, then it’s quite possible he can make a full recovery.”

The center part of the spinal cord contains the nerve fibers that execute arm function, Lau said. The leg function fibers are more on the outside of the spine, Grunch explained, “which is weird, but it is a pretty classic presentation of that type of a spinal cord injury,” she said.

Another explanation, Lau said, is that Campbell experienced spinal shock – a sudden trauma that is suppressed in the spinal cord. The inflammation resolves itself and the paralysis goes away. Patients typically recover in a day or two, Lau said.

“It’s almost like a stinger,” Lau said.

“Or,” Lau added, “he has central cord syndrome.”

‘Long’ recovery awaits Jack Campbell

Lau said it is important to distinguish between a spinal fracture – “because we could fix those problems” – and a nerve injury. The prognosis of being able to return to play or even regular activities is quite different in either scenario.

Crowning, spear tackles are dangerous because the head is pointed straight into the impact and all of the force goes straight down the spine, whereas in the back position the spine can help a person lean backward or forward, Grunch said. Lau also noted that there doesn’t have to be a high-energy collision to result in a serious spinal injury.

“If the body is in a very awkward position and is very vulnerable, even low-impact forces can cause pretty significant injury,” said Lau, who added that because Campbell’s facemask was looking up and not down at the ground, he likely avoided a worse outcome.

Returning to the field will be a massive undertaking nonetheless.

Without looking at the MRI and other imaging, Lau said, predicting a recovery timeline is difficult.

“Moving his legs completely strong is very different than being able to run or walk,” he said, adding: “You can even do leg workouts but his balance might be completely off. So recovery’s going to be long for him."

One key unanswered question at the moment is whether Campbell had any surgery performed to aid in his recovery.

“The fact of a full recovery (potential) really is very inspiring, because on the field it looked very worrisome,” Grunch said. “Return to play? To be determined.”

title: The Matthew Stafford elbow injury is a something to monitor - NBC Sports
description:
“It feels good,” Stafford said regarding what was described by the team as a right elbow injury on Wednesday.
I’m not too worried about it.” As Simms pointed out on PFT Live, elbow soreness is uncommon at this stage of the season.
It’s hard not to wonder whether the Rams disclosed Stafford as having an elbow specifically because someone finally noticed, and asked about, the ice (if, as Stafford claims, he has constantly been icing the elbow).
If it’s no big deal, why list the right elbow on the first injury report prior to the Week 9 game at Washington?
As to Stafford, it’s something to monitor.
text:
A question emerged about Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford’s throwing arm after reporters spotted ice on it following Sunday’s game against the Chargers. On Monday, coach Sean McVay called it “soreness” but otherwise deferred to Stafford for any specific questions.

On Wednesday, Stafford was asked specific questions.

“It feels good,” Stafford said regarding what was described by the team as a right elbow injury on Wednesday. “Full practice as I have been all year and hope to continue to be that way.”

So why did he have an ice pack on his elbow when he left the locker room on Sunday?

“You guys have been blind,” Stafford said with a laugh and a smile. “I feel like I’ve been icing my arm every day out here walking around. That’s on you guys. You all are the ones that are out there reporting that I have ice on my arm. Listen, I’m 38 years old trying to keep up with these young bucks. A little bit of soreness and stuff that is not uncommon this time of year. Again, I haven’t missed a rep at practice. I haven’t missed a rep in a game and I feel good. I’m not too worried about it.”

As Simms pointed out on PFT Live, elbow soreness is uncommon at this stage of the season. Quarterbacks throw less during practice in the regular season. If soreness is going to happen, it’s going to happen during training camp.

It’s hard not to wonder whether the Rams disclosed Stafford as having an elbow specifically because someone finally noticed, and asked about, the ice (if, as Stafford claims, he has constantly been icing the elbow). If it’s no big deal, why list the right elbow on the first injury report prior to the Week 9 game at Washington?

There are plenty of strategic reasons to not list an elbow issue. In 2019, the Steelers concealed quarterback Ben Roethlisberger’s elbow problem. Then, in Week 2, he suffered a season-ending, non-contact elbow injury. The Steelers and coach Mike Tomlin eventually were fined, $75,000 and $25,000, respectively, for not disclosing the elbow issue.

As to Stafford, it’s something to monitor. Especially since he’s 38 and has thrown thousands of passes. Something in the elbow is bothering him.

And it could be affecting the number of pass plays the Rams are calling during games. After throwing for more than 50 passes in Week 3 (55), Week 4 (51), and Week 5 (54), he has thrown 33 in Week 6, 29 in Week 7, and 25 in Week 8.

While, for now, it’s not impacting his ability to take his regular complement of practice snaps, it could be impacting his ability to generate maximum force and velocity on his throws. And, eventually, it could get worse.

Stafford has played through many injuries during his career. He’ll play through this one, too. Unless and until he physically can’t.

text:
With quarterback Lamar Jackson’s ninth NFL season possibly over after three full games and two first-half exits, obvious questions have emerged regarding his future in Baltimore.

The facts fuel the speculation. He’s under contract for one more season, and the Ravens can’t use the franchise tag or the transition tag to limit his ability to become an unrestricted free agent in March 2028, which is only 16 months away.

If Jackson wants a fresh start at age 31, he’ll be able to have one.

The Ravens made it clear in January that they wanted to extend his contract by the start of the new league year in March 2026. It didn’t happen, for reasons that never became clear because neither Jackson nor the Ravens (at Jackson’s behest) share information about the negotiations.

Before the season began, it seemed that a new contract wa just a matter of time. The Ravens surely would like to do it before the start of the new league year in March, when Jackson’s cap number spikes to $84.34 million. Although the team has the right to do another restructuring that would reduce the 2027 cap number, that would make the dead-cap reckoning even larger as of 2028.

A trade would avoid the final $52 million in cash and cap charges, but the cap realities would make a post-June 1 move the far better option. And there have been whispers of at least one team doing advance homework on a potential pursuit of Jackson in 2027.

The overriding question is whether Jackson’s lingering availability issue changes things for the Ravens. For now, there’s no reason to think it has. When the dust settles on the season, the Ravens will have to revisit that question.

But that will lead to another question. What would they do at quarterback without Lamar Jackson? That simple reality prompted them to give him a market-level deal in 2023, and to want to do it again.

As long as that desire to avoid a future without Lamar Jackson remains, there’s no reason to think he won’t be back in Baltimore in 2027.

text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars may have to enter Thursday Night Football without one of their top weapons.

The Jaguars released their final injury report for Thursday's Week 9 battle with the Baltimore Ravens, and it featured two big names as questionable: running back Bhayshul Tuten and defensive end Travon Walker.

There is understandable concern for both, with Walker limited in practice on Tuesday and Wednesday after sustaining a rib injury in last week's win over the Indianapolis Colts. But recent history under this Jaguars regime suggests Walker has at least a chance to play. It does not say the same about Tuten.

Jaguars History

Simply put, the Jaguars will more than likely need Chris Rodriguez Jr. to step into a starting role on Thursday based on how they have handled past injury situations. Tuten did not practice on Tuesday or Wednesday, despite Jaguars head coach Liam Coen indicating in his pre-practice press conference that Tuten would have some sort of practice activity.

“We'll see. I think he'll do something. Yeah, he'll do something," Coen said before practice. "But I would expect... I talked to him today; he said he feels better. I would think it's probably going to go up to game time.”

Instead, Tuten was a DNP for the second day in a row, which has resulted in a missed game each time during the Coen era. This is the 25th game where the Jaguars are led by Coen and his staff. In the previous 24 final injury reports, the Jaguars have had 27 instances where a player did not practice during the week. In all 27 of those instances, the player missed the game that week.

The key difference here is that Tuten is at least listed as questionable. All 27 previous instances of players missing practice led to them being outright ruled out, which of course has not been the case with Tuten. Coen has already tabbed Tuten as a game-time decision, something he has done two other times this year: in Week 1 with Cole Van Lanen and LeQuint Allen, who were each listed as questionable but played.

The difference is that Van Lanen and Allen at least practiced that week. If this was a full week and not a Thursday Night Game, which the Jaguars have not played under Coen before, perhaps things would be different. But for now, most signs point toward Tuten not being available just simply based on the Jaguars' history under Coen.

Perhaps one key that could answer the Tuten question is how Coen approached Van Lanen's status in Week 1. Van Lanen was coming off a serious knee injury that had kept him out of the entirety of training camp, though he returned in time to be limited in practice in Week 1. But a few weeks before then, here is what Coen had to say.

"I would imagine the way he would play football against Cleveland is if he practices the week of Cleveland. If he's able to practice the week of Cleveland and be able to actually feel comfortable, and feel fast and feel firm, then I'd be totally fine. But he's going to have to practice to play, absolutely.”

If that is the Jaguars' stance on injuries and playing, then history might be working against Tuten. The one thing working in his favor is that this is a short week that the Coen-led Jaguars haven't experienced before. Perhaps the wackiness of a Thursday Night Football is the X-Factor here. If not, then expect a decent amount of Chris Rodriguez Jr.

text:
Jaquan Brisker hit Deshaun Watson high on the third play of Sunday's game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cleveland Browns, drawing a roughing-the-passer flag and sending Watson to the medical tent for a concussion evaluation.

Watson was initially cleared to return and finished the game, but the situation became more serious in the days that followed. He reported concussion symptoms Monday night and was placed in the NFL's concussion protocol Tuesday morning, potentially opening the door for Shedeur Sanders to start in Week 9.

Brisker, meanwhile, appeared to dismiss concerns about the hit after Pittsburgh's win and mocked Watson's reaction. After Watson's placement in the protocol became public, NFL Media host Andrew Siciliano called out the Steelers safety for making light of a hit that sent Watson for a concussion evaluation and was later followed by concussion symptoms.

Andrew Siciliano Calls Out Jaquan Brisker After Deshaun Watson Enters Concussion Protocol

The penalty gave Cleveland a fresh set of downs on its opening possession. Watson went to the medical tent after the helmet-to-helmet hit, with Sanders taking over for four plays and finishing the drive before Watson was cleared by the unaffiliated neurotrauma consultant to return on the Browns' next offensive series.

The Browns said Watson was evaluated again after the game and on Monday morning and showed no symptoms on either occasion. However, he began experiencing symptoms Monday night, reported them to the medical staff Tuesday morning, and was immediately placed in the concussion protocol.

That development has put Watson's availability for Cleveland's Week 9 game in question. If he is not cleared to play, Sanders is in line to start against the New Orleans Saints, with Dillon Gabriel expected to serve as the backup.

BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN's Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator

Before Watson's later symptoms became known, Brisker was asked about the roughing-the-passer penalty after Pittsburgh's 27-6 victory and did not appear concerned about the hit.

"Babying the quarterback. He's over there crying or whatever he's doing. It is what it is," Brisker said.

He added another jab: "He had his binky today, so."

Siciliano, a veteran broadcaster who spent 13 seasons with NFL Network before returning to NFL Media in 2026 as host of "The NFL Report," reacted after the Browns announced that Watson had entered the concussion protocol.

SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN's Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer

"After committing a personal foul with a helmet-to-helmet hit, mocked a player who was sent for a concussion check," Siciliano wrote.

Siciliano's post came after Cleveland provided the fuller timeline of Watson's symptoms, adding another layer to Brisker's postgame remarks. Watson had passed his initial in-game evaluation and subsequent checks before developing symptoms later, illustrating why concussion concerns can extend beyond what happens immediately after a hit.

Brisker has still been productive for Pittsburgh this season. He has recorded 51 tackles through eight games and has been one of the Steelers' key contributors in the secondary. His performance can also be tracked through PFN's Safety Impact Metric.

The Sunday win also gave Pittsburgh a measure of revenge after its 27-24 loss to Cleveland on Thursday Night Football in Week 4. The Steelers improved to 6-2 with their fourth consecutive victory, while the Browns fell to 5-3.

Pittsburgh now heads into its bye week before traveling to Cincinnati to face the Bengals on Sunday Night Football on Nov. 15.

For Cleveland, the immediate focus is Watson's progression through the concussion protocol. There is no fixed timetable for clearance, and he must complete the league's return-to-participation process before playing. Until then, Sanders remains in position to make the Week 9 start if Watson cannot go.

text:
With Halloween and late sunsets in the rearview mirror and the halfway point of the NFL season hitting this weekend, we’re taking stock of our Heisman Fraternity members collecting paychecks in the NFL.

It’s been a trying time for many of our Heisman alumni in the league who have battled a bevy of ailments, some besieged by bad luck.

How else to explain 2016 Heisman winner Lamar Jackson finally returning to action on Sunday after three weeks off due to an ankle injury only to leave the game after one snap.

On his first play from scrimmage, Jackson smashed his throwing hand’s thumb on against a Buffalo Bill’s helmet badly enough that it required surgery, potentially costing him the rest of the season.

DeVonta Smith, the 2020 Heisman winner, has missed the last two games with a hamstring injury and has only suited up for four games this season.

2018 Heisman winner Kyler Murray caught the hamstring bug from Smith and injured his last week, potentially costing him his Week 9 start.

Baker Mayfield has recently returned to action after missing three games with a dislocated thumb while Jayden Daniels is recently back from a dislocated elbow injury.

Maybe we need to bubble wrap our Heisman winners.

Joe Burrow, who has dealt with more than his share of injuries, is currently healthy and thriving. He leads the NFL in passing yards per game (302.1) and touchdown passes (20) and is third in completion percentage (73.0), helping Cincinnati to a 5-2 start in a tight AFC North race.

Burrow is a game or two away from cracking the NFL’s top 100 career passing yards list and will pass Jackson soon, who is 99th.

Mayfield is the Heisman’s current acting leader in career passing yards, 62nd with 29,204 while Jameis Winston is 80th with 25,749.

Mayfield made zero headway on the passing yards chart on Sunday despite playing the entire game as Tampa Bay became the first NFL team to win a game without completing a pass since 1974. Mayfield went 0-for-3 in a driving rainstorm but directed a Buc offense that shut out Atlanta, 16-0. Whatever it takes to win.

Winston, the dean of Heisman winners in the NFL, went from backup to starter for five games with the New York Giants this fall, going 2-2-1, throwing for 957 yards and seven scores.

Like Smith and Murray, Caleb Williams has missed time — three games — with a hamstring injury. Like Burrow, he has been great while healthy, helping to lead the Chicago Bears to a 6-2 start in an NFC North that is a combined 22-8.

Williams has led the Bears to three straight wins, including back-to-back victories over last season’s Super Bowl matchup, New England and Seattle.

He has passed for 1,267 yards and six TDs and has rushed for 129, scoring twice.

Travis Hunter has been a key piece in Jacksonville’s defense as the Jaguars have raced to first in the AFC South at 5-2. He’s got 26 tackles, six deflections and two interceptions as a defensive back and seven receptions for 76 yards and a score when lining up at receiver.

Jacksonville mic’d up the entertaining second-year vet during Week 8, which is of course worth a listen.

Derrick Henry is holding down the fort in Baltimore while the Ravens deal with Jackson’s injury and others. Henry is seventh in the NFL in rushing with 632 yards and is tied for third with eight rushing scores.

He has moved into ninth on the NFL’s career rushing cart with 13,640 and is just 451 yards short of sixth place. His 130 career rushing TDs are third overall, 15 back of LaDanian Tomlinson and 34 behind Emmitt Smith.

Fourth-year Carolina Panther starter Bryce Young has cooled a bit since his hot start but is still fourth in the league in passing yards per game (274.4) and has 13 scoring passes.

Marcus Mariota has gone 33-of-51 for 340 yards and four scores in backup duty for Washington while Daniels was out.
